key_insight: Agent collaboration can achieve linear convergence up to an error floor by treating shared problem solving as block optimization with globally checked updates.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a principled way to coordinate specialized agents while checking that merged changes improve the shared objective.
method: Each agent optimizes one solution block using a local objective and a correction for cross-block effects.
A coordinator checks proposals against the global objective and merges noninterfering updates or verified combinations.
The theory bounds convergence using correction accuracy and how well accepted proposals combine.
evidence_signal: With GPT-OSS-120B on robot routing, three agents found collision-free plans in every run; on a larger task, six agents searched about twice as fast as one agent in median, while merging the best checked combination cut team search time by about 30%.
watch_item: Approximate corrections leave an error floor, and checking proposal combinations may add coordination overhead.
paper_title: Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration
